answer: The tallest Ferris wheel in the world – **High Roller** on the Las Vegas Strip – was finished and opened to the public on **March 31, 2014**. The wheel’s construction was largely completed in late 2013, with final testing and light‑up ceremonies in February 2014, and it officially began operations on that March date.

**High Roller** is a 550-foot-tall (167.6 m),[[2]]#cite_note-eastday-2)[[3]]#cite_note-heraldsun1226436835127-3)520-foot (158.5 m) diameter giant [Ferris wheel] on the [Las Vegas Strip] in [Paradise], [Nevada], United States. Owned and operated by [Caesars Entertainment] "Caesars Entertainment (2020)"), it opened to the public on March 31, 2014 as the world's tallest Ferris wheel. It is 9 ft (2.7 m) taller than the 541-foot (165 m)[Singapore Flyer], which had held the record since 2008.[[5]]#cite_note-5)[[6]]#cite_note-vitallinq-6)[[7]]#cite_note-denverpost16112011-7)[[8]]#cite_note-8) Since October 2021 it is the [world's second tallest Ferris wheel] after [Ain Dubai].

## Design

[[edit]&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Design")]

High Roller was announced in August 2011[[9]]#cite_note-9) as the centerpiece[[10]]#cite_note-10) of Caesars Entertainment Corporation's $550 million [The LINQ].[[6]]#cite_note-vitallinq-6)[Arup Engineering], which previously consulted on the [Singapore Flyer], acted as the structural engineer.[[4]]#cite_note-lvrj163776176-4)

The wheel rotates on a pair of custom-designed [spherical roller bearings], each weighing approximately 19,400 lb (8,800 kg). Each bearing has an outer diameter of 7.55 feet (2.30 m), an inner bore of 5.25 feet (1.60 m), and a width of 2.07 feet (0.63 m).[[11]]#cite_note-designnews-11)

The outer rim comprises 28 sections, each 56 feet (17 m) long. Each section was temporarily held in place during construction by a pair of 275-foot (84 m) radial struts, prior to being permanently secured by four cables.[[12]]#cite_note-12)

The passenger cabins (or capsules) are mounted on the wheel's outboard rim and are individually rotated by electric motors to smoothly maintain a horizontal cabin floor throughout each full rotation.[[13]]#cite_note-13) Preliminary designs anticipated 32 passenger cabins, each with a 40-passenger capacity[[14]]#cite_note-usatoday20110817-14)—with the final design accommodating 28 40-person cabins and a total capacity of 1,120 passengers.[[7]]#cite_note-denverpost16112011-7)[[15]]#cite_note-gjsentinel16112011-15)

Each 225-square-foot (20.9 m 2)[[4]]#cite_note-lvrj163776176-4) cabin weighs approximately 44,000 pounds (20,000 kg), has a diameter of 22 feet (6.7 m), includes 300 square feet (28 m 2) of glass, and is equipped with eight flat-screen televisions.[[16]]#cite_note-16)[[15]]#cite_note-gjsentinel16112011-15)[[7]]#cite_note-denverpost16112011-7)[[17]]#cite_note-jrn230866461-17)

At night the wheel is illuminated by a 2,000-LED system[[18]]#cite_note-forbes20140304-18) which can display a single solid color, differently colored sections, multiple colors moving around the rim,[[19]]#cite_note-reviewjournal-19) and custom displays for special events and holidays.[[18]]#cite_note-forbes20140304-18)

## Construction

[[edit]&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Construction")]

Located on Las Vegas Boulevard, across from [Caesars Palace],[[7]]#cite_note-denverpost16112011-7) construction was originally scheduled to begin in September 2011 with a late 2013 completion;[[14]]#cite_note-usatoday20110817-14) subsequently revised to early 2014.[[20]]#cite_note-vegasinc20130225-20)

The outer rim of the wheel was completed on September 9, 2013.[[21]]#cite_note-nbcnew20407248-21) The first passenger cabin was delivered and installed in November 2013 and the final cabin was installed the following month.[[7]]#cite_note-denverpost16112011-7)[[17]]#cite_note-jrn230866461-17)[[22]]#cite_note-vegasinc20131203-22) After preliminary testing, High Roller's lighting system was illuminated at sunset on February 28, 2014.[[23]]#cite_note-
